q: A 24-year-old man has a single, painless, firm penile ulcer with a clean base 3 weeks after exposure. A biopsy shows dense plasma cells and proliferative endarteritis, but no organisms on Gram stain. Why were no organisms seen?
a: C. The spirochete is too slender for Gram stain and needs silver stain or immunofluorescence
choices: A. The organism is gram-positive and stains poorly in ulcers
B. The organism is obligate intracellular and needs Giemsa to be seen
C. The spirochete is too slender for Gram stain and needs silver stain or immunofluorescence
D. The organism cannot be seen in primary lesions because it is not yet present

q: A woman has a rash on her palms and soles, silvery-gray erosions on the oral mucosa, and broad-based raised plaques in both axillae. The plaques are best called:
a: A. Condylomata lata

q: After treatment for syphilis, a patient's RPR titer falls steadily, but the FTA-ABS remains reactive. The best interpretation is:
a: B. Successful treatment; treponemal tests stay positive after cure
choices: A. Treatment failure, because FTA-ABS should become negative
B. Successful treatment; treponemal tests stay positive after cure
C. A false-positive RPR from an autoimmune disease
D. Reinfection, because both tests should fall together

q: An asymptomatic pregnant woman has a reactive RPR on routine screening. The most appropriate next step is:
a: D. Confirm with a treponemal test (FTA-ABS or TP-EIA)
choices: A. Repeat the RPR only, since pregnancy always causes false positives
B. Order PCR of blood as the confirmatory test
C. Reassure her; nontreponemal tests are too nonspecific to act on
D. Confirm with a treponemal test (FTA-ABS or TP-EIA)

q: Autopsy of a 62-year-old shows dilated aortic root with aortic valve insufficiency. Histology: obliterative endarteritis of the vasa vasorum with adventitial lymphoplasmacytic inflammation. Which complication is LEAST expected in this disease?
a: C. Aortic dissection
choices: B. Narrowing of the coronary ostia

q: A man has lightning pains in the legs, wide-based ataxia, absent knee jerks, and a painless swollen knee joint. The primary site of damage is the:
a: D. Dorsal roots and dorsal columns
choices: D. Dorsal roots and dorsal columns

q: A 50-year-old with untreated syphilis shows progressive dementia, delusions of grandeur, and frontal lobe atrophy. Brain sections show neuronal loss, gliosis, and iron deposits (Prussian blue). This is:
a: D. Paretie neurosyphilis

q: A 6-week-old infant has persistent nasal discharge, a desquamating rash of the palms and soles, hepatomegaly, and periostitis of the long bones. The mother received no prenatal care. The most likely diagnosis is:

q: A 12-year-old with an untreated congenital infection has notched, peg-shaped incisors. Which finding completes the classic triad?

q: A rubbery white-gray liver mass in a man with long untreated syphilis shows central coagulative necrosis, palisading macrophages, and many plasma cells. Treponemes are scant. This lesion is thought to arise from:

choices: D. Delayed hypersensitivity to the bacteria

q: A sexually active 20-year-old woman has lower abdominal pain, cervical motion tenderness, and new right upper quadrant pleuritic pain. AST and ALT are normal. The RUQ pain is most likely:

q: During infection, N. gonorrhoeae first attaches to epithelial cells through:

B. Culture of a swab from the site

q: A woman with gonococcal PID has several symptoms. Which is the MOST consistent symptom?
a: D. Lower abdominal pain

a: C. Haemophilus ducreyi

D. Erythromycin base 500 mg twice daily for 7 days

q: In the chlamydial developmental cycle, the form that is infectious but metabolically inactive is the:

a: B. L1-L3
